1725: Next Great Raid
1732:
The Dead far outnumber us. But each of our soldiers is far stronger than one of the Dead — numbers are beaten with command.

Counters Spearmen → trolls & wolves · Archers → ghouls & goblins · Cavalry → necromancers & goblins · Infantry → orcs
Command Pick a type with 5–9 (infantry, spearmen, archers, cavalry, all) then G charge · H retreat · J·K type skills. You can also drag-select units and right-click to move them.
Rout Units whose morale runs out flee. Units near a general or the king hold better.
1733:
The Palace is ringed by a half-circle wall, with the keep and mountains behind.

Archers shoot from the walls. They can't shoot past the walls to the far side, so move them to where the enemy masses.
Infantry & spearmen wait inside to stop enemies coming over ladders and to plug breaches. Soldiers near the wall drop stones on those below.
The Dead come with ladders, trolls and catapults. Enemies reaching the top of a ladder go for the archers on the wall first. Walls hit by catapult stones crack and then collapse — sally out with 'Open gate' to smash the catapults.
Fall If the Dead inside the walls clearly outmatch the remaining defenders for 20 seconds, the castle falls.
1735:
A village is ringed all around by a round palisade. The Dead surround it from every side, or mass where there are fewest archers.

Archers on the palisade shoot only to their front. Spread evenly they cover every side but each spot is weak; bunch them and the other side empties — watch where the enemy comes from and shift them.
Infantry & spearmen wait in the village center and strike whatever comes over or breaks through.
1736:
Defenders have a big advantage in a castle — bring plenty of troops.

Infantry are the heroes Under their shields they climb ladders fastest and fall least, then shove forward once over. Spearmen are slow and fall often.
Ram A group of spearmen pushes it into the gate. Catapults Two of them break the walls. Archers outside only hit the wall top and just inside. Cavalry wait until the gate or wall is breached, then pour through.
Beware The Dead on the walls pour firepots down on ladders and rams, and throw bone spears. Don't stand in the flames for long.
1737: The final battle. The King of the Dead wakes his minions when wounded, and goes berserk when badly hurt. Fell him and all remaining Dead waver — send your strongest units at him.
1739:
The Dead are raising ladders to climb the walls of Astera.

Archers shoot from the walls · infantry & spearmen stop whoever climbs over · you (the king) take up the sword and hold the gate.

Survive this night and the story begins.
1741: Time is frozen during deployment. When ready, 'Begin battle'.
1742: Build — raise Palace buildings. Building levels drive recruiting speed, taxes, food and population. Construction takes days; the days left show on the button. Spare gold goes here first.
1743: Recruit — one company is 100 soldiers, taking 100 people. When training ends it joins the garrison. Earn ★ with 'Drill companies' below to make it stronger.
1744: Garrison — the companies at the Palace now. They fight in defense; sending an expedition takes them from here (thinning the Palace's defense).
1745: Upgrades — one at a time, takes days. Once done it applies to all soldiers forever.
1746: Treasury — borrow gold in a pinch (10% interest a day, up to 3,000) and sell surplus food. Haggle in person at the market to sell for more.
1747: Form expedition — choose a destination, a leading general (or the king) and the companies to take, then march. The army walks the map and a battle opens on arrival. The Palace's defense thins by the companies you take.
1748: Our armies — the armies out on the map. View each one on the map or give it orders. Fatigue lowers combat power — halt on open ground to camp and recover.
1749: Generals — each has a passive and a battlefield ability (Q). Attach one to an expedition and they lead the army. Wounded generals rest a few days; fallen ones never return.
1750: Chronicle — a record of everything so far. Catch up on news you missed here.
1751: War — next Great Raid date, intel on each fort, and what to do now at a glance. Click a row to go there.
1752: Wardrobe — change the king's armor. Locked armors open with prowess, armor level, tournaments and renown. Stats are upgraded at the forge.
1753: Forge — upgrade the king's sword and armor level by level (HP and damage up; next level needs prowess). Also refill the garrison here.
1754: Treasurer — tax policy. Higher taxes bring more gold and drain favor daily. If favor reaches 0, the realm falls.
1755: Spymaster — hire spies and choose where to scout. When a spy arrives you learn enemy numbers and units; at forts, 'Infiltrate' to find weaknesses.
1756: High Priest — raise favor with gold. Low favor drives people away; at 0 the realm falls.
1757: War council — check your generals and jump straight to forming expeditions or commanding armies. ★★★ captains can be promoted to generals.
1758: Village management — village population drives taxes, food and village recruiting. Investments, walls and garrison are set here.
1759: Neighboring realms — at relations 40, trade and treaties; at 70, borrow reinforcements. Envoys are free (once every 5 days) and raise relations.
1760: Buildings — expanding and recruiting work from the Realm window too, but visiting in person grants the 'King's Visit' (a once-a-day perk per building).
1764: Prepare the realm by day 7 — the Dead's great host won't come until then (small wandering bands will)
